revision:
ONE-ROUND REVISION — preserve the current working composition and implement these bounded changes in priority order:
1. Preserve and clarify intent: Retain the dominant sphere, rich chromatic cells, dark stage, and full control panel, but make the cellular automaton legible: organize cells on a visible curved lattice or latitude/longitude topology, show clustered live/dead neighborhoods and a few emergent structures rather than uniform random scatter, and label the topology as seamless spherical wrapping. Keep every brief-required object, label, control, state, and relationship visible inside 1280×800; do not trade compliance for a cleaner crop.
2. Establish the reading structure: Bind the visualization information into one region by aligning the title directly above the sphere and grouping active cells, surface density, and topology in a compact caption immediately below it. Reposition and rescale existing elements rather than deleting them; allow one primary focal region, one supporting information tier, and quiet utility controls.
3. Finish the shared system: Mask and warp the grid and cells cleanly to the sphere, add a controlled atmospheric rim, and explicitly split orbital lines into behind/in-front segments so every intersection is intentional. Apply the correction through a small consistent set of palette, type, spacing, stroke, border, radius, shadow, and illustration rules, and repair visible clipping, collisions, weak contrast, or unfinished edges.
4. Add one content-specific expressive payoff: Carry cellular motifs into the controls through tiny state patterns, evolving swatches, and a generation pulse; vary clusters by age or lineage rather than random color alone; and add a restrained halo or orbit annotation that makes the spherical Life concept uniquely identifiable. Limit this to the hero and semantically different states; reuse the system tokens and remove arbitrary decoration so it does not create a second competing focal point.
Implementation guardrails: edit the existing self-contained HTML/CSS/JS; use no remote assets, libraries, fonts, APIs, canvas packages, or network calls. Keep the fixed viewport at 1280×800 with no scrolling. Preserve all functioning content and verify small text, edge safety, and component alignment after the revision.
conflicts: Completeness versus hierarchy: retain the fidelity action—Retain the dominant sphere, rich chromatic cells, dark stage, and full control panel, but make the cellular automaton legible: organize cells on a visible curved lattice or latitude/longitude topology, show clustered live/dead neighborhoods and a few emergent structures rather than uniform random scatter, and label the topology as seamless spherical wrapping.—while using the clarity action—Bind the visualization information into one region by aligning the title directly above the sphere and grouping active cells, surface density, and topology in a compact caption immediately below it.—to tier, group, and rescale the required material instead of removing it.

System consistency versus expression: implement the craft action—Mask and warp the grid and cells cleanly to the sphere, add a controlled atmospheric rim, and explicitly split orbital lines into behind/in-front segments so every intersection is intentional.—as the construction grammar, then permit the expressive action—Carry cellular motifs into the controls through tiny state patterns, evolving swatches, and a generation pulse; vary clusters by age or lineage rather than random color alone; and add a restrained halo or orbit annotation that makes the spherical Life concept uniquely identifiable.—only as a bounded, content-motivated hero/state exception.

One-round scope versus accumulated requests: prioritize visible requirement ambiguity and the dominant craft defect first; apply secondary typography, spacing, and decorative refinements only when they reuse the same rules and do not trigger a rebuild.
rationale: The plan preserves every requested and already working element, lets hierarchy determine prominence, uses craft rules as the implementation substrate, and admits a single semantically motivated expressive exception so one revision remains coherent and feasible.
